Thanks again for taking the time today — good conversation. Quick recap and the items we promised on the call so you have a single bucket for next steps.

- Primary goal: reduce inference latency for clinical note summarization while ensuring PHI never leaves customer-managed infrastructure.
- Scale expectation: ~3M inference tokens/month initially; bursty during daily ETL windows.
- Compliance needs: encryption-in-transit & at-rest, customer KMS, audit logs, and regional residency (US-only).

Can you confirm which attributes are must-haves vs negotiable?
2) Evidence list: Clara to share specifics on which controls are mandatory for initial POC (e.g., SOC2 type II, encryption keys in customer KMS, quarterly vulnerability scans).
3) Ops contact: assign an SRE/infra lead from MediLedger we can loop in for a short technical scoping session next week.

I've attached a brief VPC checklist we use for Private deployments and a one-pager on our Dedicated isolation controls to help you compare.

Hi Clara / team — Ben (Solutions Eng) here. Thanks for the heads-up, Kimberly. A few technical notes to set expectations before the scoping call and to make the ops checklist actionable: 

1) Private VPC model we offer (high level):
   - Control plane: for Private deployments we provide a customer-isolated control plane that can be hosted in your VPC via a transit VPC or deployed into a customer-managed subnet. Metadata routing options: (a) fully customer-hosted control plane (recommended for PHI), or (b) hybrid with strict egress controls (audit logs forwarded to S3 in your account).
2) KMS / BYOK: customer-managed cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) with HSM-backed keys is supported; we recommend HSM-backed keys if your compliance team requires FIPS-level attestations. Implementation pattern: Redwood operators request a grant/key policy at deploy time; we never hold the plaintext keys.
3) Network options:
   - VPC peering: simplest for low-latency; requires cross-account peering and route table updates.
   - PrivateLink/Interface endpoint: recommended if you cannot accept peering, provides private endpoint without broad route exposure.
   - No public internet egress: we can configure egress rules so inference workers only talk to internal endpoints and S3 buckets in your account.
4) Audit logs: we can stream per-request telemetry to your S3 bucket with configurable retention; 1 year retention is feasible. Logs include request id, timestamp, model variant, and token counts — we do not store decrypted PII in logs by default.
5) Latency: with a colocated Private deployment and optimized batching we can target p95 <= 220ms for single-turn summarization at medium batch sizes; exact SLA depends on chosen GPU profile and batching policy.

Pre-call deliverables from Redwood (I'll own these with Marissa):
- Deployment topology options (drawn diagram)
- KMS integration doc + sample grant policy
- Network checklist with peering vs PrivateLink pros/cons
- SOC2 secure link (we'll send to the secure email you provide)

Suggested agenda for the scoping call (30–45 min):
- 5m intros & objectives
- 10m control-plane & KMS model deep-dive
- 10m network topology and peering options
- 10m ops requirements and timeline to POC
- 5–10m Q&A / next steps

I'll attach the checklist we use internally as a starting point and can walk through the items live. If you prefer, we can also run a short network proof (VPC connectivity test) ahead of the POC kickoff.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
